requirement:
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
    pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
}
```

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Selector syntax is a cited requirement, so I did not reassess it. I did not need implementation source.

**Whole-file outline when a content value selects one item**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` builds a content value for the second line only, using `from_id`. It asserts that `selected.outline().items.len()` is 3, which is the root plus two lines, not one item. It also checks that `selected.select("")` returns the retained root with the full text.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the same pointer equality for a selected function.

**Root first, then items in source preorder**
- The Rust test asserts the exact selector sequence `""`, `mod[auth]`, `mod[auth]/fn[check]`, `mod[auth]/struct[Token]`, `fn[last]`. It also asserts the kinds sequence. That covers root first, parent before children, and siblings in source order.
- The Markdown tests assert nested section order, including duplicates `#1` and `#2`, and the anonymous block inside a section.
- The plain-text tests in `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` and `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` assert line order and spans.

**Full selectors identify items and their ancestry**
- The Rust test checks `mod[auth]/fn[check]`. The Markdown tests check selectors such as `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@…`. Every outline item is round-tripped through `select`.

**Root has an empty selector and covers the whole source snapshot**
- This is asserted in the Rust, Markdown, plain-text and Unicode tests. The Unicode test uses multi-byte input, so the span is checked in bytes. The empty-file case in the plain-text test also checks the root span.
- The bundled-languages test checks this for every bundled language, and also checks that item spans are valid slices of the source.

**Span includes attached source under the language's rules**
- The Rust test asserts that the `fn check` span starts at `/// Check tokens.`. It also asserts the span contains `#[inline]` and ends at the function body.
- The Markdown tests assert that setext section spans start at the original heading text and keep the container underline and body.
- Per-language attachment rules for other languages belong to the language-specific requirements, not this generic one.

Together these tests assert the required outcomes. Wrongly truncating the outline to the selected item, a wrong ordering, a missing attachment, or a wrong root would each fail an assertion. I found no unacknowledged gap.

The item's span includes its attached source under the language's rules. The
root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
